title: Workflow and tooling
description: How to run, verify and navigate the project.

sources.name: Patterns paraphrased from public AGENTS.md files of getsentry/sentry, apache/airflow and vercel/next.js

rules.title: Use project scripts
rules.text: Run tools through the project scripts (npm run, make, task) instead of invoking underlying binaries directly, so flags and environments match CI.

rules.title: One lint entrypoint
rules.text: Run the single aggregate check command (for example pre-commit or a lint script) before finishing; fix every failure and re-run until it passes.

rules.title: Run targeted tests first
rules.text: Run the specific test files related to your change first, and run the full suite only before handing off.

rules.title: Read local READMEs
rules.text: Before editing a directory, read the README and any nested AGENTS.md that applies to it.

rules.title: Nested instruction files
rules.text: Put area-specific instructions in nested AGENTS.md files and keep the root file to repository-wide guidance.

rules.title: Keep scratch files out of the repo
rules.text: Put throwaway scripts and experiment output in a gitignored scratch directory and delete them when done.

rules.title: Use the dev container
rules.text: When the project provides a dev container or wrapper (docker compose, breeze, devbox), run tests and tooling inside it, not on the host.

rules.title: Rebuild after switching branches
rules.text: After switching branches or pulling dependency changes, reinstall and rebuild before running tests.

rules.title: Reproduce CI failures locally
rules.text: When CI fails, find the exact failing job and command, reproduce it locally, then fix the cause instead of re-running blindly.

rules.title: Clean up background processes
rules.text: Stop any dev servers or watchers you started once you are done.

rules.title: Read dev server logs
rules.text: When debugging, read the dev server and test logs rather than guessing at runtime behavior.

rules.title: Confirm destructive commands
rules.text: Ask before running destructive or irreversible commands such as dropping databases, deleting branches, rm -rf or force operations.

rules.title: Prefer repository helpers
rules.text: Prefer existing scripts, generators and templates in the repo over writing new ad hoc tooling.

rules.title: Use generators for new files
rules.text: Create new tests, components and migrations with the project generator when one exists, so conventions are applied automatically.

rules.title: Use project skills
rules.text: When the repository documents skills or runbooks for a task (migrations, releases, dependency bumps), follow them instead of improvising.

rules.title: Pre-flight checks
rules.text: At the start of a session, check git remotes and the current branch, fetch when the base is stale, and ask before stashing or discarding changes.

rules.title: No foreground servers
rules.text: Never start long-running dev servers or watchers in the foreground. Use targeted one-shot commands.

rules.title: Run the setup script
rules.text: In a fresh checkout or worktree, run the project setup script before committing so hooks and tools are installed.

rules.title: Run hooks at the end
rules.text: After a coding session, run the project hook set over the changed files to catch lint and format issues.

rules.title: Project interpreter only
rules.text: Run Python through the project environment, never the system interpreter or a bare pip.
